investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent never reached a ready state, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by affinity rules and cannot be used even via preemption. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod during this eval window timed out as Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and causing all downstream evidence (vmIdPresent, remoteState, agentId, orgId) to go uncollected. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this eval failure.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 144s, endedAt 2026-07-16T20:40:06.870Z — confirms the condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 144s, endedAt 2026-07-16T20:42:35.441Z — confirms the condition persisted for at least ~7 minutes across all three checks.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — the runner never reached the agent creation step, so no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with pod scheduling failure before any agent API call could complete.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which triggers the pod scheduling path; the scheduler error surfaces before this call can return.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=132599 — the check ran for ~132s before failing, consistent with the scheduler's reported 126s unscheduled duration plus overhead.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If affinity rules were broadened or corrected, more nodes would be eligible.
Tertiary — resource quota or limit range at the namespace/cluster level capping kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations below what concurrent eval runs require.

Lower confidence — a recent infrastructure change (not reflected in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges) may have reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes or increased concurrent workload consuming those slots; no commit evidence supports this directly.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T20:37–20:42Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting zero available nodes: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval pod could not be scheduled, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state check collected no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing), causing a full contract violation.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available — 2 due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — no new remote agent pod can be scheduled. Preemption was also ruled out (no preemption victims found). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) calls createAgent with type "remote", which requires a kata peer-pod VM slot that is unavailable, so the probe times out before any evidence can be collected.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent never reached a ready state, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by affinity rules and cannot be used even via preemption. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod during this eval window timed out as Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and causing all downstream evidence (vmIdPresent, remoteState, agentId, orgId) to go uncollected. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this eval failure.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 126s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 144s, endedAt 2026-07-16T20:40:06.870Z — confirms the condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 144s, endedAt 2026-07-16T20:42:35.441Z — confirms the condition persisted for at least ~7 minutes across all three checks.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — the runner never reached the agent creation step, so no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with pod scheduling failure before any agent API call could complete.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which triggers the pod scheduling path; the scheduler error surfaces before this call can return.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=132599 — the check ran for ~132s before failing, consistent with the scheduler's reported 126s unscheduled duration plus overhead.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If affinity rules were broadened or corrected, more nodes would be eligible.
Tertiary — resource quota or limit range at the namespace/cluster level capping kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations below what concurrent eval runs require.

Lower confidence — a recent infrastructure change (not reflected in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges) may have reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes or increased concurrent workload consuming those slots; no commit evidence supports this directly.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector requirements. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 144s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-create: same Unschedulable / Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, endedAt 2026-07-16T20:37:38.048Z, latencyMs 132599 — the earliest failing check in the sequence, confirming the scheduling block predates the runtime check.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical message to remote-agent-runtime, endedAt 2026-07-16T20:40:06.870Z, latencyMs 148822 — confirms the scheduling failure persisted across consecutive probe attempts.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=148571, status=fail — the probe waited the full scheduler timeout before surfacing the error, consistent with a hard capacity ceiling rather than a transient blip.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent — the agent pod never started, so the runner could not collect any evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId — the scheduling failure occurs at this createAgent call, blocking all downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the shared scheduling dependency is the blocking layer.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the cluster has no remaining peer-pod VM slots to schedule new remote agent pods, and preemption found no evictable victims.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the remote agent pod's affinity rules, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall on those 2.

Tertiary — a concurrent workload spike or leaked/stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving none for new probe pods.

Lower confidence — a cluster scaling event (node scale-down, node NotReady, or node cordoning) that reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed to schedule one probe pod.

reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduling timeout.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all 6 cluster nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm whether kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable is 0 on the 2 affinity-matching nodes.

reproductionSteps.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep -i remote
reproductionSteps.details: Identify any stuck, leaked, or long-running remote agent pods that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

reproductionSteps.label: Check node affinity rules applied to remote agent pods
reproductionSteps.details: Review the pod spec or admission webhook for the remote agent workload to confirm which label selectors restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm shared scheduling dependency
reproductionSteps.details: If all three fail with the same Unschedulable message, the shared kata.peerpods.io/vm dependency is confirmed.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents checks fail at pod scheduling time with Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the only 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity rules. Evidence items failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state all carry the identical scheduler rejection message.

affectedAreas.label: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool on affinity-matching nodes
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports 2 nodes with Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 0 preemption victims, indicating the resource is fully consumed on the eligible nodes.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes and making the feature vulnerable to any capacity shortfall on those nodes.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918)
affectedAreas.reason: The createAgent call at line 1918 is the first point where the scheduling failure surfaces in the eval runner, preventing all downstream evidence collection and causing the full contract gap (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature registry entry — degradedAfterFailures threshold
affectedAreas.reason: features.json line 187 sets degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2. With all three checks failing, the feature will be marked degraded or in outage by the status system depending on how required vs. non-required checks are weighted.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and allocated counts on the 2 affinity-matching nodes to confirm capacity exhaustion and determine the current headroom.
Identify and terminate any leaked or stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active workloads.

Review the node affinity/selector rules for remote agent pods to determine whether the 4/6 node exclusion is intentional; if not, correcting the affinity rules would expand the schedulable pool and reduce fragility.

Evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes is sufficient for concurrent eval probe runs plus any production workloads; if not, request a capacity increase or add additional affinity-compatible nodes.

After restoring capacity, re-run the full remote-agents eval suite (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to confirm all three checks pass and the expected evidence contract is satisfied.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the eval runner that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable before attempting createAgent, so scheduling failures surface a more actionable SKIP or WARN status rather than a timeout-driven FAIL.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval to check if the scheduling failure persists
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is sustained or has self-resolved since the 2026-07-16T20:42:35Z failure window.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe all cluster nodes for kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the resource is exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes and shows current allocatable vs. allocated counts.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies any leaked, stuck, or long-running remote agent pods that are holding slots and preventing new probe pods from scheduling.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node affinity rules on the remote agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 4/6 node exclusion is intentional or a misconfiguration that is unnecessarily restricting the schedulable pool.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms that all three checks share the same scheduling dependency and fail or pass together, ruling out an isolated runner-branch defect.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable > 0 on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, the capacity exhaustion hypothesis is disproved and the cause is likely a scheduler plugin bug or misconfigured resource quota.
If a re-run of the probe immediately after the failure succeeds and schedules a pod, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are shown to also support kata.peerpods.io/vm and the affinity rules are intentionally correct, the root cause shifts entirely to capacity exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes rather than an affinity misconfiguration.

If no remote agent pods are found running or pending in the cluster at the time of failure, the capacity exhaustion is caused by something other than leaked probe pods (e.g., a reduced node count or a resource quota change).
If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks also fail with a scheduling error at the same time, the problem may be broader than the remote-agents affinity pool.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on affinity-matching nodes and warns when available slots fall below a minimum threshold (e.g., 1 slot per concurrent eval run).

Add a node-affinity-coverage check that verifies the fraction of cluster nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector rules, alerting if fewer than a configured minimum number of nodes are eligible.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that counts remote agent pods in non-terminal phases older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching capacity leaks before they exhaust the pool.
Add a preemption-readiness eval that verifies at least one lower-priority pod exists on each affinity-matching node, ensuring preemption is a viable fallback when capacity is tight.
